senses.gloss: A slight trace or hint of something.
examples: There was the faintest *suggestion* of a smile on his face.
The sauce has a *suggestion* of lemon in it.
I caught a *suggestion* of movement behind the curtain.

senses.gloss: The putting of an idea into someone's mind so that they accept it without questioning it.
examples: Half the cure was the power of *suggestion*.
The therapist used hypnotic *suggestion* to help him quit smoking.
Advertisers rely on *suggestion* far more than on facts.

senses.gloss: The person who manages an apartment building and takes care of repairs.
examples: Call the *superintendent* if the radiator stops working.
The *superintendent* lives in the basement apartment.
Our *superintendent* changed the lock the same afternoon.

senses.gloss: An exaggerated word of praise.
examples: Reviewers ran out of *superlatives* for her performance.
The coach heaped *superlatives* on his young quarterback.
The brochure is written entirely in *superlatives*.

senses.gloss: An elected member of the governing board of an American county or township.
senses.ru: член совета округа (выборная должность в США)
examples: The county *supervisors* meet on Tuesday evenings.
She was elected *supervisor* for the third district.
The board of *supervisors* voted to raise the sales tax.

senses.gloss: An extra section added to a book, a newspaper, or a report.
examples: The Sunday paper comes with a travel *supplement*.
The new findings were published as a *supplement* to the original study.
She kept the crossword *supplement* and threw the rest away.

senses.gloss: Someone who keeps going and copes well no matter what happens to them.
senses.ru: живучий человек, тот, кто не сдаётся
examples: Don't worry about her — she's a *survivor*.
He lost the business twice and started over at fifty; the man is a real *survivor*.
After the year she's had, I'd call her a *survivor*.

senses.gloss: Agreement with or support for an opinion, a group, or a cause.
examples: I have no *sympathy* for that argument.
His *sympathies* have always been with the union.
The senator is in *sympathy* with the protesters' demands.

senses.gloss: A large orchestra, or a concert that it gives.
examples: She plays second violin in the city *symphony*.
We have tickets to the *symphony* on Friday.
The *symphony* is looking for a new conductor.

senses.gloss: Eating and drinking at a party in a stadium parking lot before a game.
senses.ru: пикник у машины на парковке перед матчем
examples: *Tailgating* starts four hours before kickoff.
We brought a grill and two coolers for *tailgating*.
The lot opens early on game day for *tailgating*.

senses.gloss: A condition that helps a business or an economy make progress.
examples: Lower interest rates gave the housing market a *tailwind*.
The company expects a *tailwind* from the new tax rules.
Cheap fuel has been a *tailwind* for the airlines all year.

senses.gloss: A turnover that a defense forces in football or basketball.
examples: The defense had three *takeaways* in the first half.
That fumble was the *takeaway* that won the game.
They lead the league in *takeaways* this season.

senses.gloss: A rich, complicated mixture of many different things.
examples: The neighborhood is a *tapestry* of languages and cuisines.
Her novel weaves a *tapestry* of small-town lives.
Immigration is part of the American *tapestry*.

senses.gloss: The ideas and beliefs handed down by a religion or a great figure.
examples: The book explains the *teachings* of the Buddha.
He lived his whole life by the *teachings* of his church.
Some of these *teachings* are two thousand years old.

senses.gloss: A thin shaped piece of metal, plastic, or card that you draw or cut around as a guide.
examples: He cut a cardboard *template* for the countertop.
Trace the *template* onto the fabric before you cut.
The shop keeps a *template* for every size of window.

senses.gloss: A far-reaching branch of an organization's power or influence.
examples: The cartel's *tentacles* reach into the police department.
The agency has *tentacles* in every state capital.
By then the scandal had spread its *tentacles* through the whole company.

senses.gloss: A screen and keyboard connected to a computer, or the window where you type commands.
examples: The clerk typed the number into the *terminal*.
Open a *terminal* and run the installer.
The library still has a few old *terminals* by the door.

senses.gloss: The point on a battery or an electrical device where a wire is attached.
examples: Clip the red cable to the positive *terminal*.
Both battery *terminals* were covered in corrosion.
Make sure the *terminal* is tight before you start the engine.

senses.gloss: The area that an animal treats as its own and defends against others.
examples: The male robin defends his *territory* all spring.
Wolves mark the edges of their *territory*.
Two bucks fought over the same *territory*.

senses.gloss: The area a salesperson or a business is assigned to cover.
examples: She covers the whole western *territory*.
The new rep was given a smaller *territory*.
He drives eight hundred miles a week across his *territory*.

senses.gloss: Clear proof that something is true or that someone has a certain quality.
examples: The packed hall was a *testament* to her reputation.
That the bridge still stands is a *testament* to its builders.
His recovery is a *testament* to modern medicine.

senses.gloss: A legal document saying who should get your property after you die.
examples: She signed her last will and *testament* in front of two witnesses.
The date on the *testament* was three weeks before he died.
Under his last will and *testament*, the farm goes to his nephew.

senses.gloss: Something that serves as clear proof of a fact or a quality.
examples: The crowded gym is *testimony* to the coach's popularity.
The old barn stands as *testimony* to how carefully they built things.
Her steady hands are *testimony* to years of practice.
